key_insight: EHR-Complex is a new benchmark for testing whether medical agents can do realistic, interactive EHR reasoning rather than just generate static SQL.
clinical_relevance: It better reflects the complexity of real clinical database work, which could improve how future AI tools support EHR analysis and patient/population studies.
method: Built on MIMIC-IV with 365K patients, 31 tables, and 500M+ records.
Includes ~52K tasks across six clinical intents, covering patient-level and population-level queries.
Requires agents to interact with a sandbox by running SQL or Python, including complex longitudinal multi-table reasoning.
evidence_signal: In evaluation, the top model reached only 62.3% exact-match accuracy, and Pass^k consistency fell below 50% for nearly all models at k=4.
watch_item: Because many failures came from SQL logic, code lookup, and semantic misunderstanding, performance may still be fragile in real deployment settings.
paper_title: EHR-Complex: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Complex Clinical Reasoning
